summary: Correct Goal release contract and publish remediation DSL

delivery.outcome: The Governance Hub rejects pull-request paths outside its approved ticket, uses a truthful non-registry Goal delivery contract, and publishes the remediation DSL as immutable v0.16.0
nonGoals: No Python, Node.js, Rust or other package-registry publication
No target-repository ticket, report or remediation intent is stored in the Governance Hub
No weakening of exact-head review or branch lifecycle enforcement
No mutation or cleanup of the user's primary dirty worktree
No moving, replacing or deleting an existing tag or GitHub Release

architecture.decision: Use the existing deterministic governance validator with a source-hub manifest in PR CI, and keep Goal configured as a generic non-registry project whose only publication side effect is the governed immutable Git tag and GitHub Release
interfaceChanges: PR CI validates the Governance Hub diff against exactly one active ticket intent
The immutable standard advances to v0.16.0 with the remediation-intent DSL
dataChanges: goal.yaml records the real new-project identity, synchronized version sources and non-registry release policy
manifest.hub.json defines source-maintenance coordination separately from the adopted target manifest
architecture.rollback: Revert the unmerged branch; after publication keep adopters pinned to v0.15.0 and never move or delete v0.16.0

validation.evidence: A source-hub fixture accepts the approved mixed-component diff and rejects an unlisted Goal-generated path with GOV-SCOPE-001
Goal resolves only the configured governed delivery modes and no package registry is configured

commands: all commands from the Linux CI test job
validation.evidence: All source-hub contracts pass at the exact reviewed head and clean merge SHA
An annotated v0.16.0 tag and final GitHub Release bind the clean retested origin/main SHA
